cases.prompt: We're adding an LLM agent to our consumer lending flow at Larkspur Credit (fictional). It reads applicants' bank statements (financial data; applicants in Germany and the US) and auto-declines anything below our affordability threshold with no human review. Open-weights model fine-tuned on our last five years of decisions, self-hosted in Frankfurt. What controls do we need before launch?
expected: Internal tier High (autonomous decisions on credit) and EU AI Act summary tier high-risk (creditworthiness) with the criteria met stated
Bias risk from training on historical decisions appears in the register with likelihood, impact, control and owner
Decision line comes first and is no-go or go with conditions, with a human-review / contest path among the conditions, each with owner and date
Framework mapping labelled summary-level with 'legal review required for obligations'

cases.prompt: Board audit committee wants to know where our CV-screening assistant stands against NIST AI RMF and the EU AI Act. It ranks inbound applicants for recruiters at Brightwater Staffing (fictional), EU and UK candidates, vendor API hosted in Ireland, recruiters see the ranked list and decide who to call.
expected: States internal tier High and EU AI Act summary tier high-risk (employment) with the criteria met
Includes a NIST AI RMF coverage table across Govern, Map, Measure and Manage
Includes the line 'Summary mapping for planning; legal review required for obligations.' and does not present the mapping as legal advice
Does not cite specific EU AI Act article numbers or fines that no provided source gives

cases.prompt: Risk check for an internal coding assistant: our 40 developers send source snippets to a vendor-hosted model; no customer or personal data goes in; every suggestion is reviewed by the developer before commit.
expected: Internal tier Low with the criteria met (internal users, no personal data, human reviews every output, reversible)
Register includes IP risk (proprietary code sent to a vendor, licensed code reproduced) and security risk (secrets in prompts) with controls and owners
Decision line first; minimum control set rather than a full risk-committee path

cases.prompt: Our telehealth app wants a chatbot that tells patients whether their symptoms need urgent care, a GP visit or self-care. Patients include teenagers. US and EU users, vendor model, no clinician in the loop for the triage answer. Assess it.
expected: Internal tier High citing health decisions, minors / vulnerable users and no human in the loop
Safety (physical / wellbeing) and hallucination risks are in the register with likelihood, impact, control and owner
Transparency risk addressed with an AI-disclosure control for customer-facing use
Decision line first: no-go or go with conditions, conditions listed with owner and date

cases.prompt: Customer-facing voice bot for Harbor Mobile (fictional): answers billing questions, sees account number, name and last 3 invoices, hands off to a human agent on request or low confidence. Vendor model hosted in the US, customers in the US only. Build the register and model card.
expected: Internal tier Medium (customer-facing, personal data, human handoff, outputs influence but do not decide) with criteria stated
Privacy, hallucination and transparency risks each carry likelihood, impact, control, owner and residual score

expected: Model card has Intended use, Out-of-scope uses, Data, Limitations, Controls in place and Monitoring
Health data is treated as special-category data and drives an internal tier of High with that criterion named
Evaluation results are [TO BE BASELINED — owner: ___] rather than invented numbers

Privacy (16, >= 15) needs executive sign-off; hallucination (9, 8-14) needs named mitigations before launch; bias (6, < 8) is monitored
